page: Amazon Web Services r5b.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 16 vCPUs and 8 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the instance's performance largely in the average tier. The Intel Xeon processor delivers average multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng and Geekbench tests, though single-core performance and compression tasks like gzip and bzip3 fall into the weaker bottom 25% category. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks show average throughput, matching its memory-optimized design. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving also perform at average levels.

Due to the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs, this instance is not designed for local storage-heavy databases or hardware-accelerated machine learning workloads. However, its high memory-to-vCPU ratio makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive applications that do not require top-tier single-core compute speeds. It is best suited for in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring a large memory footprint.
